newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Bezeq Telecom Q1 results mixed.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Bezeq Telecom Q1 results mixed.

text.p: Bezeq, Israel's main telecommunications carrier, on Thursday reported a 9.3 percent decline in first quarter earnings compared with the same 1996 period, and said it was in part because last year's income had been boosted by a 32.5 million shekel insurance payment.

In addition, financial expenses in this year's quarter were higher by 73.1 million shekels to a total of 131.6 million shekels, which management attributed to the exchange rate and increased interest costs.
Bezeq said the seven percent rise in income to 2.162 billion shekels from 2.020 billion was due to higher tariffs and increased cellular telephone traffic at its Pelephone cellphone subsidiary.

"This increase was offset partly by a drop in income from international operations," Bezeq said. "The decline...came from the absence of growth in international calls combined with lower tariff income coming from North American telecom companies."
Bezeq said the number of lines grew 3.2 percent in the quarter to 45.5 per 100 population.
